fill_gaps <- function(d, keys) {
  grid <- d[, .(length_bin = seq(min(length_bin), max(length_bin), by = bin_width[1])), by = keys]
  d[grid, on = c(keys, "length_bin")]
}

# Overview

**Module 3: Repeat detection**

This module handles:

1. Finding each repeat tract in every read, between the two flank alignments and up to `rpt_flank_pad` bases into each flank (so a tract is measured in full even where the aligner placed a flank boundary inside it)
2. Checking the combined flank length of each read, with optional removal of reads whose flank length is an outlier
3. Comparing the tract lengths measured from the two strands
4. Counting each tract three ways: **full** (tract length / motif length, including any interruption inside the tract), **match** (exact motif units) and **pure** (longest uninterrupted run)
5. Recording the sequence between consecutive tracts (e.g. the CAACAGCCGCCA interruption between CAG and CCG)
6. Combined measures defined from two or more tracts (sum of units, or span from first tract start to last tract end)

**Tracts in this run:**

```{r tract_table, echo=FALSE}
dt_compact(tracts %>% dplyr::transmute(tract, motif, reference = basename(path_ref), order_in_reference = order_in_ref,
                                primary_count = count_method, min_repeats, start_perfect_repeats, end_perfect_repeats,
                                max_gap, max_tract_gap, flank_pad, reads_without_tract = na_handling))
if (nrow(composites)) dt_compact(composites %>% dplyr::transmute(measure = name, tracts, mode), caption = "Combined measures")
```

The first tract (**`r primary`**) is the primary measure: it is used for allele clustering, waterfalls and the UMI shortened-molecule filter, and its ranges in the settings file apply to every other measure that has no ranges of its own.

**Outputs:**

- `03_repeat_detection/repeat_detection.xlsx` – detection rates, count-method agreement, between-tract sequences
- `03_repeat_detection/read_repeat_counts/{sample}.tsv.gz` – one row per read with every count of every tract
- `module_data/03_repeat_detection.RData` – per-read lengths for Modules 4–7 (`alignment_counts_slim` keeps the layout older scripts use)

---

# Finding tracts

```{r detect}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
safe_load_module(file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "02_alignment.RData"), 2)
alignments <- module2_output$alignments; refs <- module2_output$refs
ref_of <- function(path) names(refs)[vapply(refs, function(r) identical(normalizePath(r$path), path), logical(1))]
group_tables <- list()
slim <- NULL
for (g in unique(tracts$ref_group)) {
  tg <- tracts[tracts$ref_group == g, ]
  rid <- ref_of(tg$path_ref[1])
  a <- alignments[[rid]]
  per_sample <- split(a, a$file_stem)
  res <- apply_fn(names(per_sample), function(s) {
    aln <- per_sample[[s]]
    rt <- process_sample_repeats(aln, tg)
    if (primary %in% tg$tract) rt <- cbind(rt, primary_segments(aln, rt, primary))
    rt
  })
  gt <- rbindlist(res, fill = TRUE)
  setnames(gt, c("ref_id", "strand"), paste0(c("ref_id_", "strand_"), g))
  group_tables[[as.character(g)]] <- gt
}
rm(res, per_sample)
read_tracts <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = c("file_stem", "qname"), all = TRUE), group_tables)
n_groups <- length(group_tables)
timings["Tract detection"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

```{r na_handling}
# Composites first, so a read missing one of the tracts has no composite value
read_tracts <- compute_composites(read_tracts, composites, tracts)
# Reads that aligned to a tract's reference but where no tract was found
for (k in seq_len(nrow(tracts))) {
  t <- tracts$tract[k]
  aligned <- !is.na(read_tracts[[paste0("ref_id_", tracts$ref_group[k])]])
  none <- aligned & is.na(read_tracts[[paste0(t, "_start")]])
  read_tracts[, paste0(t, "_found") := ifelse(aligned, !none, NA)]
  if (tracts$na_handling[k] == "convert_to_zero") {
    for (m in c("full", "match", "pure")) set(read_tracts, which(none), paste0(t, "_", m), 0)
  }
}
if (n_groups > 1 && nrow(composites) && any(composites$mode == "span")) {
  # Spans across references are only defined when both alignments put the read on the same strand
  sc <- paste0("strand_", unique(tracts$ref_group))
  diff_strand <- Reduce(`|`, lapply(sc[-1], function(s) read_tracts[[s]] != read_tracts[[sc[1]]]))
  for (nm in composites$name[composites$mode == "span"]) set(read_tracts, which(diff_strand), nm, NA_real_)
}
drop_primary <- primary_drop <- NULL
if (any(tracts$na_handling == "filter")) {
  for (t in tracts$tract[tracts$na_handling == "filter"]) read_tracts <- read_tracts[get(paste0(t, "_found")) %in% TRUE]
}
measures <- rbind(
  data.frame(measure = tracts$tract, type = "tract", motif = tracts$motif, count_method = tracts$count_method,
             definition = paste0(tracts$motif, " tract, ", tracts$count_method, " count")),
  if (nrow(composites)) data.frame(measure = composites$name, type = "combined", motif = NA, count_method = composites$mode,
                                   definition = ifelse(composites$mode == "sum", paste0(gsub("\\+", " + ", composites$tracts), " (units added)"),
                                                       paste0(composites$tracts, " (start of first to end of last)"))))
value_col <- function(m) { k <- match(m, tracts$tract); if (is.na(k)) m else paste0(m, "_", tracts$count_method[k]) }
```

## Detection rate

Each point is one sample: the percentage of its aligned reads in which **no** tract was found (so lower is better, and the axis is not capped at 100%). A tract is missing when no run of at least `min_repeats` units overlaps the region between the flanks; for a normal-length allele this should be very rare, so a high rate points to off-target product or a reference that does not match the amplicon. Detection rates per sample are in the table below and in `repeat_detection.xlsx`.

```{r detection_plot, fig.height=5}
det <- rbindlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) {
  read_tracts[!is.na(get(paste0(t, "_found"))), .(tract = t, aligned_reads = .N, with_tract = sum(get(paste0(t, "_found")))), by = file_stem]
}))[, detection_rate := with_tract / aligned_reads]
miss <- 1 - det$detection_rate
# Decimal places from the size of the largest value, so tiny rates are not all printed as 0.000%
miss_digits <- if (max(miss) > 0) max(1, -floor(log10(max(miss) * 100)) + 1) else 1
p_det <- ggplot(det, aes(tract, 1 - detection_rate)) + box_points_mean(digits = miss_digits, percent = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, NA), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = "Tract", y = "Aligned reads with no tract found", title = "Reads without a tract, per sample",
       subtitle = sprintf("%s of %s aligned reads had no tract (%s)", comma(sum(det$aligned_reads - det$with_tract)),
                          comma(sum(det$aligned_reads)), percent(1 - sum(det$with_tract) / sum(det$aligned_reads), 10^-miss_digits))) + theme_bw()
print(p_det); save_plot(p_det, file.path(plots_dir, "detection_rate.png"), 7, 5)
```

```{r pairing, eval=n_groups > 1, results='asis'}
paired <- read_tracts[, .(reads = .N, all_tracts = sum(Reduce(`&`, lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) !is.na(get(paste0(t, "_found"))))))), by = file_stem]
cat(sprintf("\n\nTracts come from %d references. %s of %s reads (%.1f%%) aligned to every reference and so carry every tract.\n\n",
            n_groups, comma(sum(paired$all_tracts)), comma(sum(paired$reads)), 100 * sum(paired$all_tracts) / sum(paired$reads)))
```

---

# Flank length

**How to read this.** The *flanks* are the parts of each read on either side of the repeat tract (the amplicon sequence, primers and UMI). Their combined length is the read length minus the tract. Every read in a sample comes from the same amplicon, so this should be almost the same in every read, and the *modal* combined flank length is the commonest value in that sample. Each point is one sample: the share of its reads whose combined flank length is exactly the modal value, or 1, 2–5, 6–10, 11–50 or more than 50 bases away from it.

This check comes straight after tract detection because the optional flank filter (`rm_flank_length_outliers`, `r if (isTRUE(params$rm_flank_length_outliers)) "on in this run" else "off in this run"`) acts here: `r if (isTRUE(params$rm_flank_length_outliers)) "reads it removes are left out of every later section and module" else "with it off, every read is kept"`.

**What it shows.** Reads 1–2 bases off are normal: single-base insertions or deletions are the commonest PacBio error, and a flank of a few hundred bases often carries one. Reads more than 10 bases off are truncated reads, chimeras or a shifted tract boundary. When nearly all reads are within a few bases, differences in read length come from the repeat itself, not from the flanks. At HTT a sample can legitimately carry two flank lengths when its alleles differ in the CCG tract, which is why the optional flank filter is off by default.

```{r flank_qc, fig.height=5}
fq <- read_tracts[!is.na(left), .(file_stem, qname, flank_total = nchar(left) + nchar(right))]
fq[, modal := { tb <- table(flank_total); as.numeric(names(tb)[which.max(tb)]) }, by = file_stem]
fq[, dev := abs(flank_total - modal)]
fq[, band := cut(dev, c(-1, 0, 1, 5, 10, 50, Inf), labels = c("exactly modal", "1 bp off", "2-5 bp off", "6-10 bp off", "11-50 bp off", ">50 bp off"))]
fband <- fq[, .N, by = .(file_stem, band)][, prop := N / sum(N), by = file_stem]
p_flank <- ggplot(fband, aes(band, prop)) + box_points_mean(digits = 1, percent = TRUE) + scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis()) +
  labs(x = "Combined flank length compared with the sample's commonest value", y = "Reads in the sample", title = "Combined flank length, per sample") + theme_bw()
print(p_flank); save_plot(p_flank, file.path(plots_dir, "flank_length.png"), 9, 5)
if (isTRUE(params$rm_flank_length_outliers)) {
  fe <- fq[, .(q1 = quantile(flank_total, 0.25), q3 = quantile(flank_total, 0.75)), by = file_stem][, iqr := q3 - q1]
  fq <- fe[fq, on = "file_stem"]
  drop <- fq[iqr > 0 & (flank_total < q1 - params$flank_iqr_multiplier * iqr | flank_total > q3 + params$flank_iqr_multiplier * iqr), .(file_stem, qname)]
  read_tracts <- read_tracts[!drop, on = .(file_stem, qname)]
  cat(sprintf("Flank length filter (%.1f x IQR) removed %s reads.\n", params$flank_iqr_multiplier, comma(nrow(drop))))
}
```

# Strand and tract length

**How to read this.** Each read was sequenced from one of the two strands of its molecule (Module 2, *Strand*). Left: the share of reads on the reverse strand at each tract length; each grey line is one sample (lengths with at least 20 reads), the coloured line is all reads pooled and the dashed line is 50%. Right: the length distribution of the reads on each strand, all samples pooled, each strand scaled to its own total so the shapes can be compared; the y-axis is logarithmic so that the tails are visible.

**What it shows.** Whether the strand a read came from affects the length measured. If both strands give the same distribution, a strand imbalance does not bias the results. If one strand runs shorter or longer, or its share changes with tract length, slippage or errors depend on the strand being copied, and samples with different strand balances are not directly comparable.

```{r strand_length, fig.height=5}
sl <- rbindlist(lapply(seq_len(nrow(tracts)), function(k) {
  t <- tracts$tract[k]; sc <- paste0("strand_", tracts$ref_group[k])
  if (!sc %in% names(read_tracts)) return(NULL)
  read_tracts[get(paste0(t, "_found")) %in% TRUE & !is.na(get(sc)), .(file_stem, tract = t, length = get(value_col(t)), reverse = get(sc) == "+c")]
}))
if (nrow(sl)) {
  sl[, w := { span <- diff(stats::quantile(length, c(0.001, 0.999), na.rm = TRUE)); if (span > 40) 5 else 1 }, by = tract]
  sl[, length_bin := floor(length / w) * w]
  s_samp <- sl[, .(reads = .N, reverse = mean(reverse)), by = .(file_stem, tract, length_bin, w)][reads >= 20]
  s_pool <- sl[, .(reads = .N, reverse = mean(reverse)), by = .(tract, length_bin, w)][reads >= 50]
  s_samp <- fill_gaps(s_samp[, bin_width := w], c("tract", "file_stem")); s_pool <- fill_gaps(s_pool[, bin_width := w], "tract")
  s_samp[, x := length_bin + (bin_width - 1) / 2]; s_pool[, x := length_bin + (bin_width - 1) / 2]
  p_sl1 <- ggplot(s_samp, aes(x, reverse)) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
    geom_line(aes(group = file_stem), colour = "grey70", alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_line(data = s_pool, colour = "#377eb8", linewidth = 1) + facet_wrap(~ tract, scales = "free_x", ncol = 1) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(x = "Tract length (units)", y = "Reads on the reverse strand", title = "Reverse-strand share by tract length") + theme_bw()
  dist_s <- sl[, .(reads = .N), by = .(tract, length, strand = ifelse(reverse, "reverse", "forward"))][, share := reads / sum(reads), by = .(tract, strand)]
  xr <- sl[, .(lo = stats::quantile(length, 0.0005), hi = stats::quantile(length, 0.9995)), by = tract]
  dist_s <- xr[dist_s, on = "tract"][length >= lo & length <= hi]
  p_sl2 <- ggplot(dist_s, aes(length, share, colour = strand)) + geom_step(direction = "mid", linewidth = 0.5) +
    facet_wrap(~ tract, scales = "free_x", ncol = 1) + scale_y_log10(labels = pct_axis()) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(forward = "#377eb8", reverse = "#e41a1c"), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Tract length (units)", y = "Share of the strand's reads (log scale)", title = "Length distribution by strand") +
    theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "top")
  p_sl <- patchwork::wrap_plots(p_sl1, p_sl2, widths = c(1, 1.3))
  print(p_sl); save_plot(p_sl, file.path(plots_dir, "strand_by_length.png"), 11, max(5, 3.2 * nrow(tracts)))
  strand_summary <- sl[, .(reads = .N, reverse = mean(reverse), median_forward = as.numeric(median(length[!reverse])),
                           median_reverse = as.numeric(median(length[reverse]))), by = .(file_stem, tract)]
} else { strand_summary <- NULL; cat("No strand information.\n") }
```

---

# Counting methods

For each read and tract, **full** counts every base of the tract (so an interruption or a sequencing error inside it adds units rather than splitting it), **match** counts exact motif units, and **pure** is the longest uninterrupted run. They agree for a clean tract. Where they differ, the tract contains either a real interruption or a sequencing error. The comparisons below are made read by read, so they need no assumption about alleles, controls or how similar the alleles of a tract are.

```{r method_agreement}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
agree <- rbindlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) {
  f <- paste0(t, "_full"); m <- paste0(t, "_match"); pu <- paste0(t, "_pure")
  read_tracts[get(paste0(t, "_found")) %in% TRUE,
              .(tract = t, reads = .N, all_agree = mean(get(f) == get(m) & get(m) == get(pu)),
                full_ne_match = mean(get(f) != get(m)), full_ne_pure = mean(get(f) != get(pu)),
                mean_full_minus_match = mean(get(f) - get(m)), mean_full_minus_pure = mean(get(f) - get(pu)),
                interrupted = mean(grepl(",", get(paste0(t, "_structure"))))), by = file_stem]
}))
# The same comparison by tract length (full count), per sample: the bin is 1 unit for
# short tracts and 5 units where a tract spans more than 40 units
by_len <- rbindlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) {
  f <- paste0(t, "_full"); m <- paste0(t, "_match"); pu <- paste0(t, "_pure")
  d <- read_tracts[get(paste0(t, "_found")) %in% TRUE, .(file_stem, full = get(f), match = get(m), pure = get(pu))]
  span <- diff(stats::quantile(d$full, c(0.001, 0.999), na.rm = TRUE))
  w <- if (span > 40) 5 else 1
  d[, length_bin := floor(full / w) * w]
  q_when <- function(x, p) { x <- x[x != 0]; if (length(x)) as.numeric(stats::quantile(x, p, type = 1)) else NA_real_ }
  d[, .(tract = t, bin_width = w, reads = .N, full_ne_match = mean(full != match), full_ne_pure = mean(full != pure),
        mean_full_minus_pure = mean(full - pure),
        # how far apart the counts are in the reads where they differ (repeat units)
        median_gap_match = q_when(full - match, 0.5), p90_gap_match = q_when(full - match, 0.9),
        median_gap_pure = q_when(full - pure, 0.5), p90_gap_pure = q_when(full - pure, 0.9)), by = .(file_stem, length_bin)]
}))
setorder(by_len, tract, file_stem, length_bin)
# The same, pooled over all samples, from the reads themselves (quantiles cannot be pooled from per-sample values)
gap_pooled <- rbindlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) {
  w <- by_len$bin_width[by_len$tract == t][1]
  d <- read_tracts[get(paste0(t, "_found")) %in% TRUE, .(full = get(paste0(t, "_full")), match = get(paste0(t, "_match")), pure = get(paste0(t, "_pure")))]
  d[, length_bin := floor(full / w) * w]
  rbind(d[full != match, .(tract = t, bin_width = w, method = "match", differing = .N, median_gap = as.numeric(median(full - match)),
                           p90_gap = as.numeric(stats::quantile(full - match, 0.9, type = 1))), by = length_bin],
        d[full != pure, .(tract = t, bin_width = w, method = "pure", differing = .N, median_gap = as.numeric(median(full - pure)),
                          p90_gap = as.numeric(stats::quantile(full - pure, 0.9, type = 1))), by = length_bin])
}))
```

## Disagreement by tract length

**How to read this.** The x-axis is the tract length of the read (the **full** count, in repeat units). The y-axis is the share of reads at that length whose **match** count (top) or **pure** count (bottom) is different from their **full** count. Each grey line is one sample; the coloured line is all reads pooled. The dashed black line is what you would expect if every base of the tract had the same small chance of a sequencing error (the fitted chance per base is given in the subtitle).

**What it shows.** The three counts agree for a clean tract and differ only when the read has an error somewhere inside the tract. A longer tract has more bases for an error to land in, so the share of reads with at least one error rises with length: 1 – (1 – *e*)^bases. When the coloured line follows the dashed line, the disagreement is ordinary sequencing error spread along the tract, and **full** is the right count, because it is not cut short by an error. A real interruption in the DNA would instead show as a step up at the length of the allele that carries it, in every sample with that allele. Lengths with fewer than 20 reads in a sample are left out of that sample's line.

```{r agreement_by_length, fig.height=5.5}
bl_long <- melt(by_len, id.vars = c("file_stem", "tract", "length_bin", "bin_width", "reads"),
                measure.vars = c("full_ne_match", "full_ne_pure"), variable.name = "method", value.name = "share")
bl_long[, method := factor(method, levels = c("full_ne_match", "full_ne_pure"), labels = c("match differs from full", "pure differs from full"))]
pooled <- by_len[, .(full_ne_match = sum(full_ne_match * reads) / sum(reads), full_ne_pure = sum(full_ne_pure * reads) / sum(reads), reads = sum(reads)),
                 by = .(tract, length_bin)][reads >= 50]
pooled_long <- melt(pooled, id.vars = c("tract", "length_bin", "reads"), measure.vars = c("full_ne_match", "full_ne_pure"),
                    variable.name = "method", value.name = "share")
pooled_long[, method := factor(method, levels = c("full_ne_match", "full_ne_pure"), labels = levels(bl_long$method))]
bl_plot <- fill_gaps(bl_long[reads >= 20], c("tract", "method", "file_stem"))
pooled_long[, bin_width := by_len$bin_width[match(tract, by_len$tract)]]
pooled_plot <- fill_gaps(pooled_long, c("tract", "method"))
# Each bin is drawn at its centre (a 5-unit bin starting at 10 covers 10-14)
bl_plot[, x := length_bin + (bin_width - 1) / 2]; pooled_plot[, x := length_bin + (bin_width - 1) / 2]
# Expected share with at least one error if each base has the same error chance e:
# 1 - (1 - e)^(units x motif length), with e fitted to the pooled line (tracts up to 150 units)
fit_e <- pooled_long[, {
  L <- nchar(tracts$motif[match(tract[1], tracts$tract)]); xx <- length_bin + (bin_width - 1) / 2; ok <- xx <= 150 & is.finite(share)
  f <- function(e) sum(reads[ok] * (share[ok] - (1 - (1 - e)^(xx[ok] * L)))^2)
  .(e = stats::optimize(f, c(1e-6, 0.05))$minimum, L = L)
}, by = .(tract, method)]
xmax_t <- pooled_plot[, .(xmax = max(x, na.rm = TRUE)), by = tract]
expected <- xmax_t[fit_e, on = "tract"][, .(x = seq(0, xmax[1], length.out = 200)), by = .(tract, method, e, L)][, share := 1 - (1 - e)^(x * L)]
e_text <- paste(sprintf("%s: %s", fit_e$tract[!duplicated(fit_e$tract)], percent(fit_e[!duplicated(tract), e], 0.01)), collapse = "; ")
p_agree <- ggplot(bl_plot, aes(x, share)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = file_stem), colour = "grey70", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = expected, linetype = "dashed", colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_line(data = pooled_plot, aes(colour = method), linewidth = 1) +
  facet_grid(method ~ tract, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#4daf4a", "#e41a1c"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(x = "Tract length, full count (units)", y = "Reads whose count differs from full",
       title = "Counting-method disagreement by tract length",
       subtitle = sprintf("Grey = one sample; colour = all reads pooled\nDashed = expected from one error chance per base, fitted (%s per base)", e_text)) + theme_bw()
print(p_agree); save_plot(p_agree, file.path(plots_dir, "count_method_agreement.png"), 10, 6)
```

## How far apart the counts are

**How to read this.** The plot above shows how often the counts differ; this one shows by how much. Only reads whose **match** (top) or **pure** (bottom) count differs from their **full** count are used. The x-axis is the tract length (full count) and the y-axis is how many repeat units lower the other count is than **full**. The solid coloured line is the median over all such reads at that length, the dashed coloured line the 90th percentile (one in ten reads differs by more), and each grey line is one sample's median (lengths with at least 20 differing reads in that sample).

**What it shows.** A single sequencing error costs **match** about one unit wherever it falls, so its line stays near 1 and rises only slowly as longer tracts collect more errors. **pure** loses everything on the shorter side of the break, so its gap grows with tract length: for a long tract with one break the median gap is about a quarter of the tract. A real interruption would give a gap of a fixed size at the length of the allele that carries it, in every sample with that allele.

```{r gap_by_length, fig.height=6}
gp <- copy(gap_pooled)[differing >= 20]
gp[, method := factor(method, levels = c("match", "pure"), labels = c("match lower than full", "pure lower than full"))]
gp[, x := length_bin + (bin_width - 1) / 2]
gp_long <- melt(gp, id.vars = c("tract", "method", "x", "length_bin", "bin_width"), measure.vars = c("median_gap", "p90_gap"),
                variable.name = "stat", value.name = "gap")
gp_long[, stat := factor(stat, levels = c("median_gap", "p90_gap"), labels = c("median", "90th percentile"))]
gs <- melt(by_len, id.vars = c("file_stem", "tract", "length_bin", "bin_width", "reads", "full_ne_match", "full_ne_pure"),
           measure.vars = c("median_gap_match", "median_gap_pure"), variable.name = "method", value.name = "gap")
gs[, n_diff := reads * ifelse(method == "median_gap_match", full_ne_match, full_ne_pure)]
gs <- gs[n_diff >= 20 & !is.na(gap)]
gs[, method := factor(method, levels = c("median_gap_match", "median_gap_pure"), labels = levels(gp$method))]
gs[, x := length_bin + (bin_width - 1) / 2]
gs <- fill_gaps(gs[, .(file_stem, tract, method, length_bin, bin_width, x, gap)], c("tract", "method", "file_stem"))
gs[, x := length_bin + (bin_width - 1) / 2]
gp_long <- fill_gaps(gp_long, c("tract", "method", "stat")); gp_long[, x := length_bin + (bin_width - 1) / 2]
if (nrow(gp)) {
  p_gap <- ggplot(gs, aes(x, gap)) +
    geom_line(aes(group = file_stem), colour = "grey70", alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_line(data = gp_long, aes(colour = method, linetype = stat), linewidth = 0.9) +
    facet_grid(method ~ tract, scales = "free") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("#4daf4a", "#e41a1c"), guide = "none") +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(median = "solid", `90th percentile` = "dashed"), name = "All reads") +
    labs(x = "Tract length, full count (units)", y = "Units lower than the full count\n(reads where the counts differ)",
         title = "How far the counting methods differ, by tract length",
         subtitle = "Grey = one sample's median; colour = all reads pooled") +
    theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "top")
  print(p_gap); save_plot(p_gap, file.path(plots_dir, "count_method_gap.png"), 10, 6)
} else cat("The counting methods agree for every read.\n")
```

## Counts against each other

**How to read this.** Each panel compares two counts for the same reads (a random subset of up to 2,000 reads per sample): the x-axis is the read's **full** count and the y-axis its **match** (left) or **pure** (right) count, both in repeat units. The colour is how many reads fall in each cell. Reads on the dashed diagonal got the same count both ways. In the **pure** panel the dotted line is half the full count.

**What it shows.** A wrong base inside a tract affects the three counts differently. **match** loses only the unit the error sits in, so its reads stay on or just below the diagonal. **pure** keeps only the longest unbroken run, so one error can cost it many units. Take a read whose tract is 100 units by the full count:

- No error: pure = 100, on the diagonal.
- One error at unit 30: the tract splits into runs of 29 and 70, and pure = 70. Depending on where the error lands, pure is anywhere from 50 (an error in the middle) to 99 (an error at an end), so reads with one error fill the space between the diagonal and the dotted half-way line.
- Two or more errors: the tract splits into three or more pieces, and pure can fall below the dotted line.

Long tracts usually carry at least one error (see *Disagreement by tract length*), so at each common tract length the reads form a vertical streak hanging down from the diagonal, and together these make the wedge. The wedge is a property of the **pure** count, not of the sample: it appears wherever there are many reads of one length. **full** is the default because it is not cut short in this way.

```{r count_scatter, fig.height=5.5}
set.seed(123)
cs <- rbindlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) {
  d <- read_tracts[get(paste0(t, "_found")) %in% TRUE, .(file_stem, full = get(paste0(t, "_full")),
                    match = get(paste0(t, "_match")), pure = get(paste0(t, "_pure")))]
  d <- d[, .SD[sample(.N, min(.N, 2000))], by = file_stem]
  rbind(d[, .(tract = t, full, other = match, method = "match")], d[, .(tract = t, full, other = pure, method = "pure")])
}))
p_cs <- ggplot(cs, aes(full, other)) + geom_bin2d(binwidth = c(1, 1)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_abline(data = data.frame(method = "pure"), aes(slope = 0.5, intercept = 0), linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey40") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", labels = comma, name = "Reads") +
  facet_wrap(tract ~ method, scales = "free", labeller = labeller(method = c(match = "match against full", pure = "pure against full"))) +
  labs(x = "full count (units)", y = "match or pure count (units)", title = "Counting methods against the full count, per read") + theme_bw()
print(p_cs); save_plot(p_cs, file.path(plots_dir, "count_methods_scatter.png"), 10, 5.5)
pure_sum <- rbindlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) {
  d <- read_tracts[get(paste0(t, "_found")) %in% TRUE, .(full = get(paste0(t, "_full")), pure = get(paste0(t, "_pure")))]
  d[, .(tract = t, reads = .N, short = mean(pure < full), median_loss = as.numeric(median((full - pure)[pure < full])),
        below_half = mean(pure < full / 2))]
}))
```

`r paste(sprintf("For %s in this run, **pure** was shorter than **full** in %s of reads; where it was, by a median of %s units, and %s of reads had **pure** below half of **full** (two or more breaks).", pure_sum$tract, percent(pure_sum$short, 0.1), format(pure_sum$median_loss), percent(pure_sum$below_half, 0.1)), collapse = " ")`

## Where the tract is broken

**How to read this.** Only reads whose tract is broken (by an error or an interruption) are used, up to 2,000 per sample. For each break, the x-axis is how far along the tract it sits, from 0% (the 5' start) to 100% (the 3' end); the y-axis counts breaks. A break is known only to the nearest unit, so it is placed at random within that unit.

**What it shows.** Sequencing errors can fall anywhere, so they give a flat spread. A **real interruption** (such as a CAA at the same place in every copy of an allele) would give a sharp spike at one position, and would mean **pure** or **match** is the more meaningful count for that tract. Breaks are fewer close to either end, because a tract must start with `r tracts$start_perfect_repeats[1]` and end with `r tracts$end_perfect_repeats[1]` perfect units (`rpt_start_perfect_repeats`, `rpt_end_perfect_repeats`): an error there shortens the tract rather than breaking it. That edge zone is a few units long whatever the tract length, so it is a large share of a short tract and a small share of a long one; how far the dips at the ends reach therefore depends on the mix of tract lengths in the run, and is not a sign of an interruption.

```{r break_positions, fig.height=4.5}
set.seed(123)
bp <- rbindlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) {
  d <- read_tracts[grepl(",", get(paste0(t, "_structure"))), .(file_stem, s = get(paste0(t, "_structure")))]
  d <- d[, .SD[sample(.N, min(.N, 2000))], by = file_stem]
  if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
  runs <- lapply(strsplit(d$s, ",", fixed = TRUE), as.numeric)
  # A break is known only to the unit, so it is placed at random within that unit; otherwise
  # short tracts (only a few possible positions) give a comb of spikes that looks like interruptions
  pos <- lapply(runs, function(r) (head(cumsum(r), -1) - stats::runif(length(r) - 1)) / sum(r))
  data.table(tract = t, position = unlist(pos))
}))
if (nrow(bp)) {
  p_bp <- ggplot(bp, aes(position)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.02, boundary = 0, fill = "#377eb8") +
    facet_wrap(~ tract, scales = "free_y") + scale_x_continuous(labels = pct_axis(), limits = c(0, 1)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
    labs(x = "Position of the break along the tract", y = "Breaks", title = "Where broken tracts are broken",
         subtitle = "Flat = sequencing errors; a sharp peak = an interruption in the sequence") + theme_bw()
  print(p_bp); save_plot(p_bp, file.path(plots_dir, "break_positions.png"), 10, 4.5)
} else cat("No broken tracts.\n")
```

```{r agreement_table}
dt_full(merge(det, agree, by = c("file_stem", "tract")), caption = "Detection and counting-method agreement per sample and tract", digits = 4)
dt_full(by_len, caption = "Counting-method agreement per sample, tract and tract length (full count bin)", digits = 4)
timings["Counting methods"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

## Modal length by counting method

The modal (most common) length of each tract per sample, calculated with each counting method over all reads. Where a sample has more than one allele this is usually the most abundant one, so the plots above are the better guide to how the methods differ.

```{r modal_by_method}
modal_method <- rbindlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) {
  read_tracts[get(paste0(t, "_found")) %in% TRUE, {
    mo <- function(x) { tb <- table(x); as.numeric(names(tb)[which.max(tb)]) }
    .(tract = t, modal_full = mo(get(paste0(t, "_full"))), modal_match = mo(get(paste0(t, "_match"))), modal_pure = mo(get(paste0(t, "_pure"))))
  }, by = file_stem]
}))
dt_full(modal_method, caption = "Modal tract length per sample by counting method (all reads)")
```

---

# Sequence between tracts

```{r between, eval=any(grepl("^between_", names(read_tracts))), fig.height=5}
bcols <- grep("^between_", names(read_tracts), value = TRUE)
between <- rbindlist(lapply(bcols, function(b) {
  d <- read_tracts[, .(file_stem, sequence = get(b))][!is.na(sequence)]
  d[, .(n = .N), by = .(file_stem, sequence)][, `:=`(junction = sub("^between_", "", b), prop = n / sum(n)), by = file_stem]
}))
between[sequence == "", sequence := "(none: tracts adjacent)"]
top <- between[, .(reads = sum(n), samples = uniqueN(file_stem)), by = .(junction, sequence)][order(junction, -reads)][, head(.SD, 6), by = junction]
between[, label := ifelse(sequence %in% top$sequence, sequence, "other")]
p_between <- ggplot(between[, .(prop = sum(prop)), by = .(file_stem, junction, label)], aes(label, prop)) +
  box_points_mean(digits = 1, percent = TRUE) + facet_wrap(~ junction, scales = "free_x") + coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = pct_axis()) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Reads in the sample", title = "Sequence between consecutive tracts",
       subtitle = "One point per sample: the share of its reads carrying each sequence (the six most common across the cohort shown)") + theme_bw()
print(p_between); save_plot(p_between, file.path(plots_dir, "between_tract_sequences.png"), 10, 5)
```

The sequence between the CAG and CCG tracts identifies the interruption structure of each read: `CAACAGCCGCCA` is the canonical allele, a duplicated `CAACAG` gives DOI, and an allele with no CAA or CCA interruption has the tracts adjacent. Per-sample proportions are in `repeat_detection.xlsx`.

# Save output

```{r save}
.t <- proc.time()["elapsed"]
lengths <- rbindlist(lapply(measures$measure, function(m) {
  vc <- value_col(m)
  read_tracts[!is.na(get(vc)), .(file_stem, qname, measure = m, length = as.numeric(get(vc)))]
}))
alignment_counts_slim <- read_tracts[!is.na(left), .(file_stem, qname, left, mid, right,
  repeat_count = get(value_col(primary)), repeat_count_full = get(paste0(primary, "_full")),
  repeat_count_match = get(paste0(primary, "_match")), repeat_count_pure = get(paste0(primary, "_pure")),
  repeat_count_tracts = get(paste0(primary, "_structure")))]
count_cols <- c(unlist(lapply(tracts$tract, function(t) paste0(t, c("_full", "_match", "_pure", "_structure")))),
                grep("^between_", names(read_tracts), value = TRUE), composites$name)
if (isTRUE(params$export_read_counts)) {
  rc_dir <- file.path(rep_dir, "read_repeat_counts"); dir.create(rc_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (s in unique(read_tracts$file_stem)) {
    x <- read_tracts[file_stem == s, c("qname", count_cols), with = FALSE]
    setnames(x, "qname", "read_id")
    # legacy columns for scripts written against Duke 2.x
    x[, `:=`(repeat_count_full = get(paste0(primary, "_full")), repeat_count_match = get(paste0(primary, "_match")),
             repeat_count_tracts = get(paste0(primary, "_structure")))]
    fwrite(x, file.path(rc_dir, paste0(s, ".tsv.gz")), sep = "\t")
  }
}
read_tracts[, c("left", "right") := NULL]
module3_output <- list(read_tracts = read_tracts, lengths = lengths, measures = measures, primary = primary,
                       tracts = tracts, composites = composites, alignment_counts_slim = alignment_counts_slim,
                       detection = det, method_agreement = agree, method_by_length = by_len, method_gap_pooled = gap_pooled,
                       strand_summary = strand_summary, modal_by_method = modal_method,
                       between = if (exists("between")) between else NULL, hash = params$module_hash)
output_path <- file.path(params$dir_out, "module_data", "03_repeat_detection.RData")
save(module3_output, file = output_path)
write_excel_function(list(tracts = tracts, measures = measures, detection = det, method_agreement = agree,
                          method_by_length = by_len, method_gap_pooled = gap_pooled, strand_by_sample = strand_summary,
                          modal_by_method = modal_method, between_tracts = module3_output$between), xlsx_path)
timings["Save"] <- proc.time()["elapsed"] - .t
```

**`r comma(uniqueN(lengths[measure == primary, qname]))`** reads with a `r primary` length passed to Modules 4–7.
